Overview

The profile begins before request release and ends after final EOF, so it contains startup, sustained service, drain, and the five-second scheduler grace. Stable-state MFU uses only the measured interval highlighted below. It is trace-verified FP4-equivalent Tensor-Core work divided by the aggregate dense B300 FP4 peak, not kernel residency or SGLang's live estimator.

Workload shape

This is intentionally simpler than the continuous-agent corpus. Every request has one fixed shape, every first token is unique, and all sockets are released from one client gate.

Requests
300 concurrent native /generate calls; attempt spread 38.9 ms.
Prompt
65,536 tokens per request, processed as 2 × 32,768-token chunks.
Generation
max_new_tokens=1. The first output token comes from prefill; the measured window contains zero decode scheduler rows.
Cache
Radix cache disabled, cache flushed before release, and a distinct first token for every request. Reported cached tokens: 0.
Offered work
19,660,800 prompt tokens. At four bytes per token ID, the raw ID arrays represent 75 MiB before JSON syntax and transport overhead.
Queue
PP0 queue depth falls from 298 to 0 across the complete 373.840-second profiler overlap. The stable interval keeps queue depth above 30; all 300 requests then drain over 368.799 seconds.
Lifecycle
First PP0 work appears at t=18.913 s. The conservative stable interval is t=20-332 s; the waiting queue reaches zero at t=366.493 s, after which only already-admitted pipeline work remains.

MFU derivation

Each 32,768-token chunk receives its own incremental numerator from the trace-anchored precision ledger. Verified routed experts count as NVFP4, candidate-score and sparse-MLA MMA as FP8, and verified attention/shared-expert GEMMs as BF16.

Fstable, FP4-eq=Σc ∈ stable PP0 chunks ΔFc = 5,306.836 PFLOP
Puseful=Fstable, FP4-eq / 312.000000 s = 17.009089 PFLOP/s
Ppeak=4 × 13,500 TFLOP/s = 54 PFLOP/s
MFU=Puseful / Ppeak = 31.498%

What the numerator includes

Expanded logical model ledger

19.839810 FP4-equivalent PFLOP per complete 65K prompt from the trace-verified Tensor-Core groups. The separate raw logical ledger is 6.969464 PFLOP; unclassified scalar, SFU, vector, and unverified work is excluded from MFU rather than assigned an invented precision.

TopK comparisons, token movement, dispatch copies, NCCL waiting, launch gaps, and profiler overhead are not counted as useful FLOPs. They can reduce MFU but cannot inflate its numerator.

Scheduler proof

Standalone decentralized PP reports zero retained running requests while one chunk per stage is active. Saturation is established by the deep positive queue, continuous stage rows, and node-local GPU telemetry rather than the inapplicable 47-running-request gate.

GPU residency and telemetry

Residency is the time a recorded kernel remains active on a GPU. Aggregate GPU-ms adds every kernel duration across ranks and streams, so overlap can push it above 4,000 ms in one wall-clock second. Active union merges overlap on each GPU first; its hard ceiling is exactly four GPU-seconds per second.

Residency is not transfer time: an NCCL kernel may stay resident while waiting for a peer or synchronizing pipeline stages. Long NCCL residency, especially on PP0, therefore cannot be read as an equally long interval of useful bytes crossing the link.

Kernel structure

The table ranks kernels by summed residency in the common window. Summed residency is useful for attribution, but it is not elapsed time: kernels on different GPUs, and occasionally different streams on one GPU, may overlap.

Why an attention kernel says decode::: that text is the CUDA implementation namespace, not the scheduler phase. SGLang selected this sparse MLA implementation for the prefill chunk shape; the scheduler evidence still shows zero decode rows in the measured window.

Method and limits

  1. The temporary pod was pinned to gpu-worker-212. A node-local guardian rejected any GPU PID whose cgroup did not contain this pod UID.
  2. A 64-token post-readiness probe verified the endpoint. The benchmark then flushed cache and released 300 pre-serialized requests through loopback.
  3. The profiler became ready before the client gate opened. It stayed active through final EOF plus a five-second scheduler grace, rather than stopping at a fixed duration.
  4. The analysis window starts at the last rank's profiler start and ends at PP0's first profiler stop. This is the interval in which every PP rank is simultaneously eligible for capture.
  5. The stable interval is the longest contiguous interval whose trailing 15-second PP0 chunk rate stays within 10% of the deep-queue median, every PP stage logs work in every second, and queue depth stays above 10% of the offered request count (minimum 16). The full timeline remains visible so this selection can be audited against startup and drain.
  6. MFU is a model-level lower-bound estimate under the stated precision-aware FP4-equivalent convention and dense B300 FP4 peak. It is not Tensor Core instruction utilization, achieved occupancy, or a claim that every operation executes as NVFP4.
